record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: For the outer billiard about an oval γ, periodic trajectories define an area spectrum given by the areas of the associated extremal circumscribed polygons. Is this area spectrum related to the spectrum of some differential operator, analogously to how the billiard length spectrum is related to the Dirichlet Laplace spectrum by the Poisson summation formula?

evidence.quote: Is this area spectrum related to the spectrum of some differential operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let γ be a smooth, strictly convex closed curve (an oval) in the plane R². The outer (dual) billiard map T_γ is defined on the exterior of γ as follows: for a point p outside γ, there are two tangent lines from p to γ; choosing (say) the right tangent line and letting q be the point of tangency, define T_γ(p) to be the reflection of p through q, i.e. T_γ(p) = 2q − p.

A point p is N-periodic if T_γ^N(p) = p and the orbit visits N distinct tangent points q_1, …, q_N on γ. To each such periodic orbit one associates the circumscribed N-gon with vertices p, T_γ(p), …, T_γ^{N−1}(p) (whose sides are tangent to γ at q_1, …, q_N). For each integer N ≥ 3 and each rotation number, consider the extremal (e.g. minimal-area or maximal-area) circumscribed N-gons tangent to γ corresponding to N-periodic orbits, and let A_N(γ) denote the collection of areas of these extremal circumscribed polygons. The set

  Spec_area(γ) := { A_N(γ) : N ≥ 3, all admissible rotation numbers }

is called the area spectrum of the outer billiard about γ.

For comparison, in the case of the ordinary (inner) Birkhoff billiard inside a convex domain Ω, the length spectrum (lengths of periodic billiard trajectories) is related, via a Poisson-type summation formula, to the spectrum of the Dirichlet Laplacian on Ω.

Question: Does there exist a (linear) differential operator D_γ, naturally associated to the oval γ, whose spectrum is related to the outer-billiard area spectrum Spec_area(γ) by an analogue of the Poisson summation formula linking the Dirichlet Laplace spectrum to the inner-billiard length spectrum?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any construction of a differential operator whose spectrum is related, via a Poisson-type summation formula, to the outer-billiard area spectrum of an oval. Recent work (e.g. studies of outer/symplectic length billiards and Ivrii-type conjectures for outer billiards) treats related spectral-rigidity questions but does not resolve this analog of the inner-billiard length-spectrum/Dirichlet-Laplacian correspondence. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Starting the study of outer length billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Periodic trajectories' perimeters are special cases of the marked length spectrum for outer length billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work initiates spectral study of outer billiards via length, not area; no operator analog is given for the area spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on outer billiard periodic orbits continues, without producing a Poisson-type formula linking the area spectrum to a differential operator.
